questions.question: In which city is the Eiffel Tower?
questions.explanation: It was finished in 1889. Visitors can climb the stairs to the second floor or take a lift all the way to the top.

questions.question: In which city can you see Big Ben?
questions.explanation: The famous clock tower is part of the Houses of Parliament, on the bank of the River Thames.

questions.question: The Statue of Liberty stands in the harbour of which big city?
questions.explanation: France gave the statue to the USA as a gift in 1886. She holds a torch high in the air.

questions.question: In which country is the Great Wall?
questions.explanation: The wall was built over many hundreds of years to help keep out enemies. Parts of it are very old.

questions.question: In which country are the Pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid was made from millions of huge stone blocks. Workers had no big machines.

questions.question: In which city is the Colosseum?
questions.explanation: It was built almost 2,000 years ago. The big oval building has many arches and could hold a huge crowd.

questions.question: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: A Mughal emperor built it in the 1600s. Thousands of workers took many years to finish it.

questions.question: In which country is the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
questions.explanation: The tower began to lean when only a few floors were built. It was finished almost 200 years later.

questions.question: The Sydney Opera House stands beside a harbour in which country?
questions.explanation: Its roof is made of big curved shapes that look like white sails or shells.

questions.question: Which country has the huge Christ the Redeemer statue on a hill?
questions.explanation: The statue looks out over the city of Rio de Janeiro with its arms stretched wide.

questions.question: In which country is Machu Picchu, an old city high in the mountains?
questions.explanation: The city sits high in the Andes mountains. It was built about 600 years ago.

questions.question: Which city has the statue of the Little Mermaid by the water?
questions.explanation: The statue shows the girl from Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale. It was put on a rock in the harbour in 1913.

questions.question: In which country is the ancient stone circle Stonehenge?
questions.explanation: Huge stones stand in a ring on a grassy plain. The biggest stones were put up about 4,500 years ago.

questions.question: Neuschwanstein, the fairy-tale castle on a hill, is in which country?
questions.explanation: The castle looks like it comes from a story. It is said to have inspired the Sleeping Beauty castle at Disneyland.

questions.question: In which country is the Grand Canyon?
questions.explanation: Water slowly cut this huge valley through the rock over millions of years. In places it is more than 1.5 kilometres deep.

questions.question: Which bridge over the River Thames can lift up in the middle for tall ships?
questions.explanation: The two halves of the road lift up like gates. The bridge opened in 1894.

questions.question: The orange-red Golden Gate Bridge is in which city?
questions.explanation: The bridge's colour is called International Orange. It opened in 1937.

questions.question: In which city is the Parthenon, a ruined temple on a hill?
questions.explanation: It was built almost 2,500 years ago in ancient Greece. Its marble columns can be seen from far across the city.

questions.question: In which country is the stepped pyramid of Chichen Itza?
questions.explanation: The pyramid has stairs on all four sides. It was built about 1,000 years ago in the jungle.

questions.question: The big white Hollywood sign overlooks which city?
questions.explanation: The sign sits high on a hill. Film studios grew up in the area around it.

questions.question: St Basil's Cathedral, with colourful onion domes, stands on Red Square in which city?
questions.explanation: It was built in the 1500s. The bright domes look like patterned sweets.

questions.question: The Statue of Liberty is green. Why?
questions.correct: Its copper has turned green over time
wrong: It was painted green when built
It is covered in green moss
It is made of green stone
questions.explanation: The statue is covered in thin copper. Air and rain slowly turn copper green, just like old copper roofs.

questions.question: Why did the ancient Egyptians build the great pyramids?
wrong: As towers to watch for enemies
questions.explanation: A pharaoh was buried inside with food and treasure for the life after death.

questions.question: The glass pyramid outside the Louvre museum is in which country?
questions.explanation: The Louvre is a huge art museum in Paris. The glass pyramid is its main entrance.

questions.question: In which city do guards in red coats and tall furry hats stand outside Buckingham Palace?
questions.explanation: The guards march out in a ceremony called the Changing of the Guard. Many tourists watch it.

questions.question: Uluru is a giant red rock in the middle of which country?
questions.explanation: Uluru glows deep orange and red at sunrise and sunset. It is sacred to the Aboriginal people of the area.

questions.question: Which material is the Eiffel Tower made of?
questions.explanation: The tower is painted again every seven years to stop the iron from rusting.

questions.question: The Blue Lagoon, a warm milky-blue pool to swim in, is in which country?
questions.explanation: The water is heated deep underground by hot volcanic rock. It is rich in minerals.

questions.question: What is the London Eye?
questions.explanation: People ride in glass pods that turn slowly high above the River Thames and see the whole city.

questions.question: In which city is the Empire State Building?
questions.explanation: The building has 102 floors. It was finished in 1931.

questions.question: Which fighters put on shows in the Colosseum in ancient Rome?
questions.explanation: Some gladiators were slaves and some chose to fight. Large crowds came to watch them.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal is built mainly from shiny white what?
questions.explanation: Many gems are set into the marble. Its colour seems to change from pink at dawn to gold at sunset.

questions.question: Which country has the CN Tower, a very tall tower with a glass floor?
questions.explanation: Visitors can stand on the glass floor and look straight down. The tower is a landmark of the city of Toronto.

questions.question: The Forbidden City, a huge old palace for emperors, is in which city?
questions.explanation: Emperors lived there for almost 500 years. It has many halls and courtyards inside high red walls.

questions.question: The Alhambra, an old palace and fortress on a hill, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Its name comes from an Arabic word meaning 'red'. The walls have a red-brown colour.

questions.question: The White House, where the US president lives and works, is in which city?
questions.explanation: It was finished in 1800, and John Adams was the first president to live there.

questions.question: Which big Australian city has a steel bridge nicknamed 'the Coathanger'?
questions.explanation: The bridge has a huge arch and opened in 1932. It stands close to the Sydney Opera House.

questions.question: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the USA as a present?
questions.explanation: It was a gift of friendship from the French people. The statue was shipped across the Atlantic in pieces and put up in 1886.

questions.question: The Pyramids of Giza stand at the edge of a desert, close to which big Egyptian city?
questions.explanation: Giza is now part of Greater Cairo. The pyramids are on the edge of the desert, west of the Nile.

questions.question: What was the Louvre in Paris before it became a museum?
questions.explanation: The Louvre began as a fortress and later became a palace for French kings. It became a museum in 1793.

questions.question: In which city is the Brandenburg Gate?
questions.explanation: The old stone gate was built in the 1700s. It is one of the best-known symbols of the city.

questions.question: The rose-red city of Petra, carved into cliffs, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Its most famous building, the Treasury, is carved into a rock wall at the end of a narrow gorge.

questions.question: Which city has the Hagia Sophia, a famous domed building near the Blue Mosque?
questions.explanation: Istanbul lies in both Europe and Asia, on either side of the Bosphorus strait.

questions.question: In which city is the Sagrada Família church?
questions.explanation: Work on the church began in 1882 and has taken more than a hundred years.

questions.question: Mont-Saint-Michel, an abbey on a small rocky island, is in which country?
questions.explanation: The sea comes in fast around the island at high tide, so visitors must watch the time.

questions.question: The Giant's Causeway, with thousands of stone columns, is on the coast of which part of the UK?
questions.explanation: The columns are made of basalt, which formed when hot lava cooled millions of years ago.

questions.question: Which country has the Petronas Twin Towers?
questions.explanation: The two towers are joined by a bridge high in the air. They stand in the city of Kuala Lumpur.

questions.question: The Charles Bridge, an old stone bridge lined with statues, is in which city?
questions.explanation: Thirty statues line the bridge, which was begun in 1357.

questions.question: The Atomium is a giant model of an iron crystal. In which city is it?
questions.explanation: Its nine shiny balls are joined by tubes with stairs and escalators inside.

questions.question: Cappadocia is known for its rock towers and hot-air balloons. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: People once cut homes and churches into the soft rock, and even dug whole towns underground.

questions.question: Tradition says that if you throw a coin into the Trevi Fountain in Rome, you will do what?
questions.correct: Come back to Rome one day
questions.explanation: The custom is to throw it with your right hand over your left shoulder. Thousands of coins land in the water every day.

questions.question: The Vasa, a royal warship from the 1600s, can be seen in a museum in which city?
questions.explanation: It was raised from the sea floor in 1961, more than 300 years after it sank. Most of its wood is original.

questions.question: The Vigeland sculpture park, with over 200 statues of people, is in which city?
questions.explanation: Many of the statues show people of all ages, from babies to old people.

questions.question: The Old Town of Dubrovnik, with its thick stone walls, is beside the Adriatic Sea in which country?
questions.explanation: Visitors can walk along the old walls and look over red roofs and the sea.

questions.question: Monasteries on top of tall rock pillars at Meteora are in which country?
questions.explanation: The name Meteora means 'high in the air'. Monks climbed up the rocks hundreds of years ago.

questions.question: The huge Palace of Versailles lies just outside which French city?
questions.explanation: French kings once ruled from this palace. Its Hall of Mirrors is world famous.

questions.question: Schönbrunn Palace, once an emperor's summer home, is in which city?
questions.explanation: The palace has more than 1,000 rooms and a large garden with a maze.

questions.question: Teotihuacan, with its Pyramid of the Sun, lies near which big city?
questions.explanation: It was a great city more than 1,500 years ago, long before the Aztecs.

questions.question: In 1889, the Eiffel Tower was built as the entrance to which kind of event?
questions.explanation: The fair marked 100 years since the French Revolution. The tower was meant to be taken down after 20 years.

questions.question: What is the name of the great bell in London's Elizabeth Tower?
questions.explanation: Many people call the whole tower Big Ben, but the name belongs to the heavy bell inside it.

questions.question: Only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World survives. Which one?
wrong: The Statue of Zeus at Olympia
questions.explanation: It is also the oldest of the seven. The other six were destroyed long ago, mostly by earthquakes and fires.

questions.question: The Grand Palace, with golden spires and colourful roofs, is in which Asian city?
questions.explanation: Building began in 1782. The famous Temple of the Emerald Buddha stands inside its walls.

questions.question: Belém Tower, an old stone fort at the water's edge, is in which city?
questions.explanation: Portuguese explorers set sail from near here on long voyages by sea.

questions.question: Hadrian's Wall, built by the Romans, runs across the north of which country?
questions.explanation: The Romans began building it about 1,900 years ago. Soldiers guarded the northern edge of their empire.

questions.question: The Gateway of India, a stone arch beside the sea, is in which Indian city?
questions.explanation: The arch was built in the early 1900s and stands by the harbour.

questions.question: Ha Long Bay, with thousands of limestone islands, is in which country?
questions.explanation: The islands rise out of the green sea like towers, and many have caves inside.

questions.question: The Cliffs of Moher, tall sea cliffs on the Atlantic coast, are in which country?
questions.explanation: The cliffs rise high above the waves. Seabirds such as puffins nest there.

questions.question: The Nazca Lines are giant drawings of animals in the desert of which country?
questions.explanation: The lines show shapes like a monkey and a hummingbird. They are best seen from the air.

questions.question: The Burj Al Arab, a hotel shaped like a sail, stands by the sea in which city?
questions.explanation: It stands on its own small island, joined to the shore by a bridge.

questions.question: The Merlion, a statue with a lion's head and a fish's body, is a symbol of which Asian country?
questions.explanation: The name Singapore comes from words meaning 'Lion City'.

questions.question: Waitomo Caves, lit by thousands of glow-worms, are in which country?
questions.explanation: The glow-worms light the cave roof like a night sky. Visitors drift through in small boats.

questions.question: Legend says that if which birds ever leave the Tower of London, the kingdom will fall?
questions.explanation: The Tower keeps ravens and has an official keeper, called the Ravenmaster, who looks after them.

questions.question: The church Hallgrímskirkja has a tall tower that is a landmark in which Nordic capital?
questions.explanation: Its shape reminds many people of columns of basalt rock formed by lava.

questions.question: The Parthenon in Greece was built as a temple for which goddess?
questions.explanation: Athena was the goddess of wisdom and the protector of Athens. A huge statue of her once stood inside the temple.

questions.question: Chillon Castle stands on a rock at the edge of Lake Geneva. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: The castle is near Montreux, at the eastern end of the lake, with the Alps rising behind it.

questions.question: The Rialto Bridge crosses the Grand Canal in which city?
questions.explanation: The stone bridge was finished in 1591 and has shops along it.

questions.question: Himeji Castle, nicknamed the White Heron, is in which country?
questions.explanation: The castle's white walls and roofs look like a bird with open wings. It is about 400 years old.

questions.question: Why does the Tower of Pisa lean?
questions.correct: The ground under it is soft
wrong: It was built crooked on purpose
questions.explanation: The soil on one side could not hold the heavy tower. Engineers have since stopped it leaning further.

questions.question: The royal palace Gyeongbokgung, built in 1395, is in which Asian city?
questions.explanation: It was the main palace of the Joseon kings, who ruled Korea for about 500 years.

questions.question: The huge square Jemaa el-Fnaa, full of storytellers and food stalls, is in which Moroccan city?
questions.explanation: It lies at the heart of the old walled town, the medina. Snake charmers and musicians also perform there.

questions.question: Which African country is named after a medieval stone city whose ruins stand in it?
questions.explanation: The name Zimbabwe comes from a word for 'stone houses'. The city was built about 800 years ago.

questions.question: Sigiriya, an ancient palace on top of a huge rock, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Sigiriya is also called Lion Rock. A king built his palace there about 1,500 years ago.

questions.question: Borobudur, a huge temple shaped like a stepped mountain, is in which country?
questions.explanation: It was built more than 1,000 years ago and was covered by jungle and ash for centuries.

questions.question: The Wieliczka mine, with chapels and statues carved from salt, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Visitors walk down hundreds of steps. Even the chandeliers in the chapels are made of salt crystals.

questions.question: Tutankhamun's tomb was found in the Valley of the Kings near which Egyptian city?
questions.explanation: Howard Carter found the tomb in 1922. Many pharaohs were buried in the valley.

questions.question: Most of the stone-and-brick Great Wall seen near Beijing was built under which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Earlier walls were mostly made of packed earth. The Ming used much more stone and brick, which is why their wall is the best kept.

questions.question: The Terracotta Army was buried to guard the tomb of which ruler?
questions.explanation: He was the first emperor of China. Farmers found the clay army by chance in 1974.

questions.question: What was the original name of the Colosseum?
questions.explanation: It was named after the Flavian family of emperors. 'Colosseum' probably comes from a giant statue that stood nearby.

questions.question: Most of Stonehenge's smaller 'bluestones' came from hills more than 200 km away, in which country?
questions.explanation: Most came from the Preseli Hills. Each weighs a few tonnes, far less than the giant sarsen stones.

questions.question: Which explorer made Machu Picchu famous around the world after reaching it in 1911?
questions.explanation: Local farmers already knew the site. Bingham's photographs and articles told the world about it.

questions.question: Which Indigenous people are the traditional owners of Uluru?
questions.explanation: The Anangu have lived around Uluru for thousands of years. They share its stories and care for the land.

questions.question: The Colossus of Rhodes, one of the Seven Wonders, honoured which Greek god?
questions.explanation: Helios was the sun god. The statue fell in an earthquake only about 50 years after it was finished.

questions.question: In ancient Greece, people travelled to Delphi to ask advice from what?
questions.explanation: The priestess was called the Pythia. People believed she spoke for the god Apollo.

questions.question: The Fisherman's Bastion, with white towers and a view of the Danube, is in which city?
questions.explanation: It looks like a fairy-tale castle, but it was built around 1900 as a terrace for views.

questions.question: The Great Mosque of Djenné, famous for being built of mud, is in which country?
questions.explanation: By tradition, the people of the town add a new layer of mud each year to protect the walls from the rain.

questions.question: Which ancient people carved the tombs and temples of Petra out of the rock?
questions.explanation: They grew rich from trade in spices and incense. Their capital lay in a hidden valley.

questions.question: The Turkish name Pamukkale, for white terraces of mineral pools, means what?
questions.explanation: Warm spring water leaves a white mineral crust on the hillside, so the terraces look like cotton.

questions.question: For which king was Neuschwanstein Castle built in the 1800s?
questions.explanation: Ludwig II was nicknamed the Fairy-Tale King. He died before the castle was finished.

questions.question: The old wooden wharf houses of Bryggen are in which Norwegian city?
questions.explanation: German merchants of the Hanseatic League once traded from these buildings.

questions.question: The ruins of Carthage, the ancient rival of Rome, are in which modern country?
questions.explanation: The ruins lie by the sea near the city of Tunis. Carthage and Rome fought three wars.

questions.question: The mud-brick fortified village of Aït Benhaddou, used in many films, is in which country?
questions.explanation: It stands on an old trade route across the Sahara. Its clay buildings need regular repairs.

questions.question: The Banaue rice terraces, cut into steep hills by hand, are in which country?
questions.explanation: They were built by the Ifugao people and are watered by streams from the forests above.

questions.question: The old walled port city of Cartagena de Indias is in which South American country?
questions.explanation: Thick stone walls were built to protect the city from pirates.

questions.question: Hampi is full of ruined temples and palaces from the Vijayanagara Empire. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: Huge boulders lie scattered among the ruins, giving the place a strange look.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal stands on the banks of the Yamuna River in which Indian city?
questions.explanation: Agra was a capital of the Mughal emperors in the 1500s and 1600s.

questions.question: The Roman aqueduct of Segovia, with two rows of arches, crosses the old town. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: The aqueduct is made of huge stone blocks that are held together without any mortar.

questions.question: The ruined Greek and Roman city of Ephesus, with its Library of Celsus, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Ephesus was a busy port, and its Temple of Artemis was one of the Seven Wonders.

questions.question: At Ellora in India, the Kailasa temple was carved out of what?
questions.explanation: Workers carved it from the top downwards, cutting it out of a hillside.

questions.question: In Russian, what does the word 'kremlin' mean?
questions.explanation: Many old Russian cities have a kremlin. The best known stands in Moscow.

questions.question: Which dynasty built most of the Alhambra's palaces in Granada?
questions.explanation: The Nasrids were the last Muslim rulers in Spain. Their kingdom ended in 1492.

questions.question: Why were most Egyptian pyramids built on the west bank of the Nile?
questions.correct: The setting Sun was linked to the dead
wrong: The stone was easier to find there
The river flooded the east bank
The west bank was nearer the sea
questions.explanation: The Egyptians saw the west, where the Sun goes down, as the land of the dead. The royal tombs at Thebes are on the west bank too.

questions.question: The Bridge of Sighs in Venice links the Doge's Palace to what?
questions.explanation: Prisoners crossed the covered bridge after their trial. The name comes from the sighs they were said to make.

questions.question: The sea fortress Suomenlinna lies off the coast of which Nordic capital?
questions.explanation: Sweden began building the fortress in the 1700s, when Finland was part of Sweden.

questions.question: In which decade did the Sydney Opera House open?
questions.explanation: Building took about 14 years, from 1959, and cost far more than planned.

questions.question: Skellig Michael, a rocky island with an early monastery, is off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: Monks lived there for hundreds of years and built stone huts shaped like beehives.

questions.question: The ruined temples of Ayutthaya, once the capital of a kingdom, are in which country?
questions.explanation: Ayutthaya was a rich trading city for about 400 years until it was burned in 1767.

questions.question: The Hermitage museum, once the Winter Palace of the Russian tsars, is in which city?
questions.explanation: Peter the Great founded St Petersburg in 1703. The palace's green-and-white building stands beside the River Neva.

questions.question: Why were the temples of Abu Simbel in Egypt cut into pieces and moved in the 1960s?
questions.correct: A new dam would flood them
wrong: A new road was planned there
questions.explanation: The Aswan High Dam made Lake Nasser. Workers lifted the temples to higher ground, block by block.

questions.question: The Golden Pavilion, a temple covered in gold leaf that shines in a pond, is in which Japanese city?
questions.explanation: Its Japanese name is Kinkaku-ji. Kyoto was Japan's capital for over a thousand years.

questions.question: The Pont du Gard, a Roman bridge with three tiers of arches, carried water as part of an aqueduct in which country?
questions.explanation: It crosses the River Gardon and brought water to the Roman city of Nîmes.
